investigation.title: local-agent-runtime eval failure: LLM provider overload returned 502 at POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test
investigation.summary: The local-agent-runtime eval check failed with a 502 bad_gateway because the upstream LLM provider returned an overloaded_error during the runtime/test call, causing the harness to surface the error as an invalid event shape rather than a successful completion. All required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent from the eval result because the provider call never completed successfully, so the expected-output contract is entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The upstream LLM provider was overloaded at the time of the eval run (2026-08-31T06:35:26–06:36:01Z). The harness runtime test endpoint POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test received an overloaded_error event from the provider, classified it as an invalid event shape, and returned HTTP 502 with error code bad_gateway. Because the LLM call did not complete, the probe received no response payload, leaving all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) unpopulated and the message assertion ("hello from aura") unverifiable. This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by transient provider capacity, not a confirmed user-facing product outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.title: harness-skill-invocation: Installed skill not surfaced in agent context during real chat turn (skillInContext=false, textMatches=false)
investigation.summary: The eval check harness-skill-invocation failed because the installed skill was not present in the agent's context window during the real project chat turn, and the agent's response did not contain the expected probe phrase "AURA_SKILL_PROBE_OK". Skill creation and installation both succeeded (created=true, installedOnAgent=true), isolating the failure to the skill-context injection or agent-inference layer rather than the skill management APIs.
investigation.rootCause: The root cause is uncertain but is localized to the skill-context delivery path: after a skill is successfully installed on an agent, the runtime harness or the project chat session layer failed to inject the skill's instructions into the agent's active context for the chat turn. Evidence shows skillInContext=false and textSample="" (empty response body), with an "error" frame present in the stream, indicating the chat turn either errored before the model could respond or the skill context was not forwarded to the model. This is an eval-layer failure against the desktop-release runtime on desktop-nightly-macos-aarch64; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream observability eval failed because the OpenAI API account used by the eval runner has no remaining credits, causing the upstream image generation call to be rejected with error code credit_balance_exhausted. The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of the required generation_completed frame, and no image URL was produced, causing both contract assertions to fail.
investigations.rootCause: The OpenAI API key configured for the eval environment has an exhausted credit balance (error type: insufficient_quota, code: credit_balance_exhausted). When the eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream, the upstream OpenAI request was rejected immediately, causing the server to emit a generation_error frame with GENERATION_FAILED instead of completing the stream with a generation_completed frame and an artifact URL. This is an external dependency (billing) failure scoped to the eval environment's API credentials, not a code defect in the image generation stream routing logic itself. No evidence of a user-facing production incident is present in the supplied packet.
